parameters.content:
## Monitor foreclosure listings by ZIP with Google Sheets and Gmail

Create a daily property watchlist using Foreclosure Finder on RapidAPI, Google Sheets and Gmail. Choose a ZIP, radius setting, price range and minimum bedrooms. This template helps developers and automation builders follow foreclosure and REO search results.

### How it works

One request searches Auction.com, HUD HomeStore, Fannie Mae HomePath, Freddie Mac HomeSteps and Redfin. The workflow validates the response, compares source-plus-listing-ID keys with a dedicated Google Sheet, and saves unnotified matches. Gmail sends one digest when email is enabled; accepted sends are recorded in the sheet.

The first email includes existing unnotified matches. Later runs suppress previously notified source records. History does not continuously refresh availability or alert on price changes.

### Setup

Connect your own [RapidAPI subscription](https://rapidapi.com/claytoncloudsolutions-claytoncloudsolutions-default/api/foreclosure-finder1), Google Sheets and Gmail credentials. Copy the included header row, enter your settings, preview with email disabled, then test to your inbox before activating. The export starts inactive; its daily schedule defaults to 8 a.m. America/New_York.

### Limits

One run supports at most 500 matches. Oversized or reported partial scans stop before writes or email. Coverage varies; verify property status and pricing at the source. Run one execution per sheet at a time and inspect Sent after uncertain failures.

Provided by Foreclosure Finder, the API provider. Built with AI assistance.

## 1. Create your dedicated watchlist sheet

Create a Google spreadsheet and name its tab **Watchlist**. Copy the tab-separated header from the large note below into A1. Do not add a title row. Keep one row per listing_key and one workflow per dedicated sheet.

## 2. Fill Watchlist settings

Set your ZIP, radius, minPrice, maxPrice, minBeds and propertyType. Set spreadsheetId to the ID between /d/ and /edit in your Google Sheets URL; set sheetName to Watchlist. Set recipient to one inbox you control. Keep **sendEmail=false** initially.

## 3. Connect RapidAPI

Subscribe to Foreclosure Finder using the link in the yellow description. In **Search five sources**, create/select **Generic Credential Type → Header Auth**. The credential header name is **X-RapidAPI-Key**; its value is your own subscribed API key. X-RapidAPI-Host is already set. Keep your key in Credentials, never in the workflow or URL.

## 4. Connect Google

Choose your Google Sheets OAuth credential in **Read watchlist history**, **Save pending matches**, and **Mark matches notified**. Use the same account/document/tab. In both write nodes, keep **Column to Match On = listing_key** and **Cell Format = Let n8n format (RAW)**. If prompted, refresh the columns from your sheet header.

Connect your Gmail credential in **Send watchlist email**. n8n Cloud offers Google sign-in; self-hosted installations need [Google OAuth setup](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/credentials/google/oauth-single-service/).

## 5. Preview before sending

Keep the workflow inactive and **sendEmail=false**. Run **Test manually**. The workflow saves pending rows to your sheet, then stops at **Release email if enabled** without sending. Inspect the recipient, subject and message in **Build email preview**, plus the sheet rows. No new/current pending matches means the run stops earlier with no email.

## 6. Test one send and a repeat

Set **sendEmail=true** and run manually to your own inbox. Confirm one digest arrives and the sheet records notified_at and gmail_message_id. A message ID means Gmail accepted the send; checking your inbox verifies receipt. Run again against unchanged results: previously notified matches should not generate another email. The first email includes every current unnotified match, so use narrow filters for a small first digest.

## 7. Activate the schedule

Check **Workflow settings → Timezone** and **Daily at 8 AM**. The default is daily 08:00 in **America/New_York**, observing daylight saving time. Change both settings as needed, then publish/activate. Do not overlap manual and scheduled executions.

## Validation status of this preview

Exported Code nodes passed fixture tests for empty/partial responses, 500/501-result boundaries, deduplication and retry handling. A live RapidAPI response with 24 matches passed transformation and repeat-run checks on September 9, 2026 (Eastern). That count is a dated check, not promised inventory.

**Google Sheets writes and Gmail sends were simulated. An authenticated n8n import and Google-connected end-to-end test still need to pass before this template can be described as production-validated.**

## Stage 1 · Search your market

**Test manually / Daily at 8 AM → Watchlist settings → Validate settings → Search five sources**

Your settings choose the ZIP and filters. Validation catches missing setup before a request. One authenticated RapidAPI call searches all five sources. The schedule runs only after activation.

## Stage 2 · Find unnotified records

**Validate complete scan → Read watchlist history → Find unnotified matches**

Incomplete, failed-source or oversized scans stop here. Complete scans compare source + listing ID with the sheet. Already notified records are skipped. Empty results stop without a digest.

## Stage 3 · Save pending matches and preview

**Save pending matches → Build email preview → Release email if enabled**

Persist the whole pending batch before sending. Preview shows the exact recipient and message. **sendEmail=false** saves pending rows but sends nothing; it is not a read-only dry run.

## Stage 4 · Send and record acceptance

**Send watchlist email → Confirm delivery → Mark matches notified**

Send one digest, then save Gmail’s message ID and notified_at. Gmail acceptance is not proof of inbox receipt. After an uncertain send or failed final write, inspect Sent before retrying.

## Paste this exact header into cell A1 of your Watchlist tab

The code block below contains one line with real tabs between all 15 column names. Copy that line and paste into Google Sheets A1. It should fill A1:O1. If it stays in one cell, use **Data → Split text to columns → Detect automatically**. Do not copy the code fences.

```text
listing_key	source	listing_id	address	price	bedrooms	bathrooms	property_type	asset_type	status	property_link	first_seen	last_seen	notified_at	gmail_message_id
```

Keep these column names unchanged. The three Sheets nodes use this schema. No other file or external header download is required.

## One complete watchlist, at most 500 matches

One ZIP with a radius setting; source coverage/search areas vary. One API request per run, approximately 28–31 scheduled requests/month plus tests. Larger, incomplete or reported partial-source responses stop before sheet writes or email: narrow the filters to fit. This version does not paginate. Cached data can be about one hour old. Check failed executions in n8n; there is no separate error email.

## History and pending sends

The sheet keeps first-observed source records, not a live availability list. The same property on different sources can have separate rows. New and pending current matches are saved before email. A Gmail message ID confirms acceptance, not inbox receipt. Accepted sends receive notified_at. Previously notified rows do not create alerts for later price changes.

Pending matches retry only while still present in a complete scan. A disappeared pending record remains in history and is not emailed as a current match. A source silently reporting zero listings cannot be distinguished from empty inventory.

## One execution at a time

Do not overlap manual/scheduled runs or share this sheet between workflows. Gmail acceptance and Sheets updates are separate operations. After an uncertain send or failed final write, inspect Gmail Sent and the execution before retrying: a duplicate digest is possible. Do not enable automatic Gmail retries.

## Verify source inventory

Auction and other source inventory can include private-seller auctions or ordinary listings. Check asset_type, status and the original listing. An opening bid is not a final purchase price. Confirm availability, terms and property details at the source.

## Keep account details private

This template has no API key, recipient address, personal Sheet ID or pinned execution data. After configuring your own copy, remove credentials, personal settings and execution/pinned data before exporting it for other people. Share the clean generated template instead. Never publish API keys.

## Provider and costs

Maintained by Foreclosure Finder, the API provider. Basic listing fields used here are available on the free API plan; check current quotas and overage settings on [RapidAPI](https://rapidapi.com/claytoncloudsolutions-claytoncloudsolutions-default/api/foreclosure-finder1). n8n hosting may have separate costs. Paid-only valuation and yield fields are not required for this workflow.
